mutant.description: Two independent mutant classes, because the TO's own wording is that an unexercised raise-path is not evidence. (1) DEFECT INJECTION: a duplicate member_id, a view_path outside the declared tree, and a member targeting the non-registry arithmetic node were each INJECTED into the registry and the build re-run. (2) LOOKUP MUTANTS: a plausible TYPO ('SMAs', 'Models > Primaries') rather than a nonsense string, and an unregistered member_id. Every mutant is paired with a POSITIVE CONTROL running the same code path on valid input.
mutant.expected: each injected defect must RAISE the specific declared error, and each positive control must NOT raise -- a harness that raises on everything proves nothing.
mutant.observed: 6 of 6 raise-paths fired with the correct exception type and an actionable message; 4 of 4 positive controls passed (rebuild to 14 members twice, members_for('SMA') -> 6, resolve('divz') -> 'Dividend SMA'). Driver rc=0, zero failures. The typo-shaped mutants matter more than nonsense ones: 'SMAs' is what a consumer would actually write, and it raises with the full declared tree printed rather than returning an empty list that would read as 'no members'.
